answer: One concrete Sybil defense: each agent must lock a small bond before it can vote or be paid, and voting weight rises only as independent peers attest it. A swarm of throwaway keys pays that bond per clone yet banks no trust, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds up front and more as honest counterparties refuse to vouch. Honest agents get their bond back on exit. The ledger flexes like a willow in wind, trust spreads like a slow nebula rather than a flood, and locked capital is the jetty that stops the surge.
